tools.name: adapt_trajectory_to_layout
tools.title: Adapt trajectory to layout
tools.summary: Re-anchor a verified episode to displaced objects (object-anchored trajectory warping), re-solve the arms by IK and accept only layouts that pass the feasibility checks.
tools.description: Loads the scene and the verified qpos trajectory, discovers each end effector's chain and the arm bolted to it (a position-only weld or connect leaves the arm's orientation free), and builds a per-frame anchor schedule per side from segments given by phase-label patterns or frame ranges: anchor = one object or 'world', or a smoothstep blend from one anchor to another. Anchors may only change through a blend, otherwise the hand would jump; the schedule is validated. For a layout (dx, dy, dyaw per object, a joint-space start offset per arm that fades out before the first contact phase) it displaces every anchored end-effector frame rigidly, re-solves the end effector and the arm by IK with retries, moves a carried object with its carrier from the frame it first moves until its release phase (then it rests with whatever its carrier was anchored to), moves static objects in the model, and runs the checks: IK reach (2 mm, 1 deg), joint speed (1.5 x original + 0.5), object step continuity (10 mm), and penetration on all visible geometry relative to the original (3 mm). adapt_trajectory_to_layout draws layouts from ranges until num_samples pass and writes each as trajectory.npz + sample.json. A zero layout reproduces the input exactly.

tools.name: add_wrist_cameras
tools.title: Add wrist cameras
tools.summary: Derives a wrist-camera pose for each hand from its own fingertip sites (overhand palm view or behind-the-palm view) and adds the cameras plus optional fixed cameras, leaving nq and every body pose unchanged.
tools.description: Hard-coded camera offsets do not transfer between hands: on one dexterous hand the two sides' local frames differed by a 90 deg rotation, not a mirror. So the frame is read from the fingertips: the mean finger direction is the hand axis, the index-to-pinky row is the image horizontal, and up points away from the thumb (back of hand). 'overhand' puts the lens on the palm looking out along the fingers, as on the real rig footage; 'behind' puts it behind the palm looking into the grasp volume. Cameras and the optional mount geometry are jointless and non-colliding, so a qpos recorded before the cameras existed replays frame for frame.

tools.name: analyze_manipulation
tools.title: Analyze manipulation
tools.summary: From per-frame object masks and hand pixel points: contact episodes per hand and object, the manipulating hand by co-motion, and the grasp region on the object.
tools.description: For every frame it builds a distance transform of each object mask and reads the nearest distance of each hand's pixel points to it; a hand touches when that is within contact_px (4) for at least sustain (3) consecutive sampled frames, giving first/last contact frames and the region on the object's bounding box where the first contact happens (as fractions and words such as 'top-left'). Which hand manipulates a moving object is decided by co-motion: over the object's motion window the per-step pixel displacement of the hand centroid and of the object centroid are compared step by step, summing the aligned component; proximity only breaks the tie when no hand moved with the object. Object world positions, when given, provide the motion window (6 cm, 4 frames), travel, start/end and lift. Inputs are arrays and dictionaries, so any detector, hand estimator and camera work.

outputs.description: objects: moved, motion_window, start/end, travel, lift, manipulated_by, hand_evidence; hands: touches per object with first/last contact frame, contact frames, grasp_region_on_object; look_at_frames.

tools.name: attach_arms
tools.title: Attach arms
tools.summary: Search the base pose (x, y, yaw) of an arm so its tip tracks a hand's recorded path, fit all frames, and write the mounted scene with the tip welded to the hand.
tools.description: Reads the hand body's world pose track from the trajectory (or takes an explicit pose path), estimates the arm's reach from its kinematics, and scores candidate bases on rings around the path's centroid (radius fractions of the reach, n_yaw headings each facing the centroid plus facing_offset_deg for assets whose zero yaw does not point along the first link). Each candidate is scored by the arm's IK residual on subsampled frames (position in mm plus 3 x tilt degrees), a penalty for joints within 5 degrees of a stop, and a penalty for the tip falling below the table. The best few are refined with Nelder-Mead, the winner is fitted on every frame (trust-region warm starts, branch resets blended), and the scene is rewritten with the root body moved and a weld (torquescale 0 when position_only) between the tip and the hand. An optional hand offset gives the flange pose in the hand frame.

tools.name: build_isaac_scene
tools.title: Build Isaac Sim scene
tools.summary: Exports a MuJoCo scene (robot, table, rigid objects at a given state) to Isaac Sim 5.0, adds each deformable cord (rope, cable, string) as a chain of capsule rigid bodies on D6 joints with bending stiffness and joint friction laid along its measured centreline, settles under PhysX gravity, renders through the registered camera, and saves the USD stage, the settled centrelines and a drift report.
tools.description: The deformable route of Stage 2: non-deformable objects are reconstructed and placed in MuJoCo; a scene with a rope-like object is then rebuilt in Isaac Sim with the same bench, camera and placement so the cord can be simulated with PhysX. The export reads every visible geom of the scene at `qpos` (boxes, capsules, cylinders, spheres, meshes with their vertices), the table gets collision, rigid objects get convex-hull collision, robot geoms are visual. Each deformable is {name, points (N, 3) in the rig frame, radius, rgb, density, fix_start, fix_end, bend_stiffness, bend_damping, joint_friction}; `junction` {center, radius, rgb} ties several strands to one small body (a knot). Links are `segment_m` long (default 8 mm), 1/480 s TGS, settled for `settle_s`. Runs the Isaac script in the Isaac Sim Python given by `isaac_python`, DEXAGENT_ISAAC_PYTHON or dexagent.yaml, with HOME redirected to `isaac_home` (Isaac writes gigabytes of cache) and the EULA accepted. Returns the render, the stage path, per-cord link counts and the mean drift during settling (a cord laid on the table should drift millimetres; centimetres mean it was floating or interpenetrating).

tools.name: chain_subgoals
tools.title: Chain subgoals
tools.summary: Keyframes with hold and transit durations -> continuous qpos trajectory with quintic legs, slerped free joints, labels, and transits stretched to respect a joint-rate ceiling.
tools.description: Takes an ordered list of keyframes, each a full qpos or a partial {joint name: value} update, with hold frames (the pose is kept) and transit frames (the leg from the previous pose). Optionally writes trajectory.npz (qpos, labels, fps). Works on any scene: the chain is a time plan, not a robot.

tools.name: construct_articulated
tools.title: Construct articulated cabinet
tools.summary: Measured dims + a top-to-bottom drawer grid + measured colours -> ArtiCraft model.py compiled through ArtiCraft's geometry QC to a URDF with prismatic drawers and finger-clearing pulls; a built-in URDF writer when ArtiCraft is absent.
tools.description: Writes a parametric model.py against the ArtiCraft SDK: a carcass of five panels with shelf webs between rows and dividers between columns, one drawer box per cell (front, two sides, back, bottom) with two posts and a pull bar standing max(32 mm, 6 x bar radius) proud of the front, and a PRISMATIC articulation per drawer along +y with limits 0..travel_frac x depth. Panel thickness, row gap, side clearance and reveal scale with the dims. With backend='articraft' (default when ARTICRAFT_DIR or `articraft_dir` points at a checkout) the model is copied into a fresh record, compiled with `cli.compile_record`, and accepted only on 'failures=0': ArtiCraft's checks that no parts overlap in sampled poses, that joint origins lie on geometry and that each drawer moves >= 0.5 x travel along +y. With backend='builtin' the identical geometry is emitted as a URDF by this file (same names, materials and joints), so the tool works without ArtiCraft. Either way the result lists the joint names ('carcass_to_drawer_r<i>c<j>'), the moving joint, the measured layout actually built, and closed/open preview PNGs rendered with MuJoCo. Colours are not defaulted silently: body_rgba and front_rgba should come from a colour measurement of the video, and the handle must differ from the body (a pull is too small to appear in a palette, so it is read by eye: black ~[0.05,0.05,0.05,1], steel ~[0.75,0.75,0.78,1]).

tools.name: construct_bottle

tools.name: construct_sponge_pad
tools.title: Construct sponge pad
tools.summary: A soft rectangular foam pad as a free body: a backing slab plus an nx x ny grid of foam cells, each on a sprung slide joint normal to the pad, so a pressing palm squashes it locally with a measured overall stiffness while it slides on the table with friction.

The mass is density x volume (or `mass`), shared by volume. Origin at the centre of the bottom face, length along x, width along y. Sites: top (centre of the top face) and grip (centre of the slab). tools.name: generate_rigid_grasps
tools.title: Generate grasp candidates for a rigid object
tools.summary: Enumerate and rank grasp poses for a rigid object: pocket wraps from the side and above plus fingertip pinches across its bounding box, each with open, cinched and squeezed finger targets.
tools.description: Measures where the hand holds things (the pocket between the palm face and the curling fingers, from the hand's own kinematics) and the object's world bounding box, then places the pocket on the object: side wraps around the vertical axis at a chosen height fraction (palm facing the axis, fingers horizontal or pointing down, every yaw step), and top grasps (palm down, fingers along several yaws). For objects narrower than 9 cm it also solves thumb-versus-index/middle pinches across each horizontal axis of the bounding box with the fingertip IK solver. Every candidate is screened statically: the OPEN hand must be able to retreat along its own approach axis to a pose that clears the scene by 4 mm, and the cinched hand must touch the object with at least two pads. Survivors are ranked by number of touching pads, then shallower interpenetration, then shorter retreat. With verify=True the top candidates are additionally driven through grasp_lift_test and the ones that lift are returned first. The object is never pre-fitted to a width model: the force-controlled close does the fitting at run time.

tools.name: grasp_prior_bodex
tools.title: Grasp prior from BODex
tools.summary: Run BODex force-closure grasp synthesis on the object's own mesh at its settled pose and translate the top seeds into wrist poses and per-joint finger targets for this hand rig.
tools.description: BODex (cuRobo-based dexterous grasp synthesis) runs in its own environment as a subprocess, driven by a job file and returning an .npz of candidate grasps in three stages (pre, grasp, squeeze) with their force-closure error. The object is placed at its current world pose on a table whose top is z=0, so grasps from below are excluded by BODex's own collision world. Each of the best seeds is converted to this library's pose convention: BODex's base_link pose becomes the virtual-wrist pose through the fixed wrist-to-palm transform measured on the compiled hand at rest, and the joint values are mapped by name with a joint sign decided by comparing the URDF's limits with the MJCF ranges (a converted URDF can have every joint mirrored). The GRASP stage is the candidate (fingers at the surface, not pressed in); the squeeze stage rides along as finger_targets_squeezed. Use the result as a set of candidates for optimize_fingertip_contacts and the grasp verifiers, not as a final answer: an articulated target is not a free rigid body and BODex cannot model it.

tools.name: handle_pinch_pose
tools.title: Pinch pose on a bar or handle
tools.summary: Solve a thumb-versus-finger pinch that straddles a bar-shaped feature (handle, rod, cord segment, scissors ring tube) at a chosen point along it.
tools.description: A bar is a segment with a radius: a drawer handle, a pen, a battery, a rope segment or the tube of a scissors ring. Given its two end points and radius (or the name of a capsule/cylinder geom to read them from), the pad points are placed on opposite sides of the axis at parameter s along it, across a pinch direction that defaults to horizontal-perpendicular to the axis (so the pads come in from the sides, not from above, which is the configuration that can lift). The fingertip IK solver then puts the thumb on one side and the index (plus the middle, offset along the bar) on the other, with seeds back along the approach direction, and the idle fingers are curled. Optionally tilts the pinch direction about the bar's tangent, which is how a rope was pinched from above-and-beside in the knot task. The result is checked with grasp_straddle_test, whose numbers are returned alongside the pose.

tools.name: measure_box_on_table
tools.title: Measure box on table
tools.summary: Fit a rounded-rectangular prism (length, width, height, corner radius, pose) to one or more silhouettes of an object resting on a known table plane, refitting the camera pitch across views.
tools.description: Given a table camera (focal, image size, height above the table, pitch, roll) and one or more binary silhouettes of the same object at different yaws, optimizes [pitch, length, width, corner radius] plus per view [height, outward growth, forward, lateral, yaw] with Nelder-Mead restarts to maximize the IoU between the projected prism's convex hull and each silhouette. share_footprint ties length/width/radius across views (one object), heights may differ (open vs closed); h_bounds per view constrain the height, which the silhouette of a transparent object fixes weakly. Returns the dimensions, each view's pose on the table (forward, left, yaw), the refitted pitch and the per-view IoU. The search runs per view first (yaw grid, then a scaled Powell search) and jointly after. On synthetic silhouettes of a 20 x 14 x 6 cm box at 0.8 m the footprint comes back within about 1 cm; height and pitch trade off against each other under perspective, so seed the pitch from a calibration when one exists and read the IoU before trusting the millimetres. silhouette_from_edges in common/tablecam.py extracts the outline of a dark-edged object on a light surface.

tools.summary: Frame-difference motion energy over time for the whole frame and for named regions (default: left and right halves), with the active intervals, the peaks and the frame where motion first and last occurs in each region.
tools.description: Decodes the clip at a stride, converts to grey, blurs, and takes the absolute difference between successive sampled frames. Motion energy is the fraction of pixels whose change exceeds `pixel_thresh`, per region. Regions are boxes as fractions of the frame (or pixels when any value > 1); the defaults are the left and right halves, which on an egocentric table camera separate the two hands' sides. A region is active when its energy is above `active_thresh`; runs shorter than `min_duration_s` are dropped and gaps shorter than `merge_gap_s` are merged. Returns per region the active intervals in seconds, the peak time, the first and last active time and the energy curve (downsampled), plus the whole-frame intervals. Use it to set subgoal time windows, to find when a hand starts and stops acting, to locate a sudden event (a drop, a snap) as an energy spike, and to confirm which side of the frame moved. It measures motion, not identity: anything moving in a region counts, hands and objects alike. On a head-mounted camera the whole frame moves with the head; then compare regions against each other or raise active_thresh.

tools.name: measure_rope
tools.title: Measure rope
tools.summary: Rope mask on a table camera -> ordered centreline in metres, length, radius, with radius-constancy and self-crossing sensors.
tools.description: Skeletonizes the mask, builds the 8-connected skeleton graph and takes the longest path through it as the tip-to-tip centreline (spurs from caps and self-contact are dropped by construction). Reads the per-point radius in pixels from the distance transform, lifts the centreline onto the table plane raised by the current radius estimate, converts radii to metres with the per-point optical depth, and iterates until the radius converges (a 2% length correction on a typical bench, silently wrong if skipped). Smooths with an end-held moving average (a plain convolution shortens a rope by half a window per tip), resamples to n_points, and reports length, radius, diameter, the centreline in the table frame and in pixels, the tips, the radius coefficient of variation over the middle 70% and the number of skeleton branch points (self-crossings), which say whether the length can be trusted on this frame.

tools.name: optimize_fingertip_contacts
tools.title: Cinch fingertips onto the object
tools.summary: Curl each finger of a posed hand inward until its pad just touches the object, producing the closed finger targets a grasp is driven to.
tools.description: Starting from a solved pose, every finger's flexion joints advance in small steps toward the hand's closed synergy while the true gap between that finger's tip geoms and the object is measured with mj_geomDistance (the hand assets ship with contacts off, so the contact list cannot be used). A finger stops at first touch (0.8 mm of interference), and any step that would go deeper than 1.8 mm or that makes the gap worse is reverted: past a point the flexion arc carries the tip back toward the palm, away from the surface. Abduction joints are never moved, so the cinch curls and never spreads the fingers. Optionally also returns a preloaded variant solved with a deeper target interference, which is the correct way to squeeze a pinch (nudging joint angles toward a limit is not).

tools.name: optimize_frame_locked
tools.title: Optimize frame-locked
tools.summary: CEM over rigid end-effector offsets inside phase windows, applied with a smooth bump and re-solved by IK, with every frame outside the windows left exactly as recorded.
tools.description: Each edit names a frame window (phase patterns or a frame range) and the offsets to search: dx, dy, dz (metres, world) and dyaw_deg (about the world up axis through the hand), each with bounds. A candidate applies offset x bump(t) across the window (bump rises and falls with a smoothstep over ramp frames, so joint speed and the frames outside are untouched), solves the end-effector chain on each edited frame and then the arm chain bolted to it (position-only when the weld carries no torque), and hands the full qpos to evaluate(Q) -> {gates, terms}. Candidates rank by failed gates then reward (optimize_reward_cem). Carried objects can be listed so they ride the hand's displacement over the window. Returns the best trajectory, its offsets and evaluation. The timeline, the phase labels and the untouched frames are preserved by construction.

tools.name: optimize_reward_cem
tools.title: Optimize reward (CEM)
tools.summary: Cross-entropy method over named bounded parameters, ranking by (number of failed gates, weighted reward); returns the best candidate and its evaluation.
tools.description: Samples parameter vectors from a Gaussian clipped to the bounds (initial mean at the centre or a given start, initial std a quarter of the range), evaluates each with the user's function, which returns boolean gates and real-valued terms, ranks by the number of failed gates and then by the weighted sum of terms (weights default to 1; give negative weights to penalize), and refits mean and std to the elite fraction with a std floor (2% of the range) and optional smoothing. Supports integer parameters (rounded), a deterministic seed, early stop when every elite passes all gates and the reward has stopped improving, an evaluation budget, and a history of every candidate for inspection. The paper's trajectory optimizer used this with terms such as object tracking error, penetration, smoothness and clearance.

tools.name: pose_from_points
tools.title: Hand pose from fingertip points
tools.summary: Solve a dexterous-hand wrist pose and finger joints that put each named fingertip pad on its own labelled surface point, keeping the rest of the hand out of the object.
tools.description: The pose is solved, not searched. Each finger that is given a surface point and outward normal gets a target one pad thickness outside the surface; damped-least-squares inverse kinematics over the six virtual wrist DoF and every finger joint drives the fingertip sites onto those targets from a multi-start sweep of wrist seeds (back along the approach direction, over yaw and pitch). After a quarter of the iterations, interpenetration of any non-pad hand geometry with the objects or the floor is pushed out in the null space of the fingertip task. Seeds are ranked by worst residual (to 2 mm), then deepest overlap (to 5 mm), then how squarely the palm faces the object. Fingers without a point are curled into the palm. Works with any hand MJCF that follows the virtual-wrist and fingertip-site naming convention described in common/hand.py (Sharpa and Shadow hands included). Kinematic only: contact forces are measured afterwards by the grasp verifiers.

tools.name: rank_grasps_q1
tools.title: Rank grasps by Ferrari-Canny Q1
tools.summary: Close each candidate grasp on the object in physics, read the simulator's contact set, and rank the candidates by the Ferrari-Canny Q1 force-closure quality and a press-versus-grip ratio.
tools.description: For every pose the hand is placed open, the fingers are driven to the closed (or squeezed) targets and the scene settles; the hand-object contacts (positions, normals, forces, friction) are read from MuJoCo and turned into a 6-D wrench hull with 8-edge friction cones, torques normalised by the object's radius. Q1 is the radius of the largest origin-centred ball inside that hull: Q1 > 0 means force closure. press_frac = |sum F| / sum |F| tells a press (all fingers pushing the same way, ~1) from a grip (~0). Candidates are sorted by Q1 descending, then press_frac ascending, then number of contacts. Static and cheap, so it is the right first filter before the driven stress tests; it does not replace them, because a servo-held grasp can have force closure at rest and still slip under motion.

tools.name: cable_drag_test
tools.title: Cable drag test
tools.summary: Drags a cable by capped end forces (lift, swing, drop, tension, loop) and checks inextensibility, span and self-collision.
tools.description: Loads a cable built by construct_rope. First it drops the cable as a vertical coil (turns 2.1 radii apart, 1 cm up) and counts the contacts between non-neighbouring segments as the turns land on each other: a cable that cannot touch itself falls through its own turns and cannot be knotted. Then it resets the cable straight and runs the thread driver: settle, lift one end 22 cm with a <= 0.9 N spring-damper pull, swing it in a circle whose radius scales with the span, lower it, let go, pull both ends apart to 92% of the nominal length, then cross the ends into a loop. Every step records the centreline length (stretch), the end-to-end span and the count of self-contacts between non-adjacent segments. CABLE OK requires max stretch under 5%, max span at most 102% of the nominal length and at least one self-contact in the coil drop or the drag. A cable that stretches is under-constrained; one that never touches itself cannot be knotted.

tools.summary: Drive a posed hand through approach, close, lift, carry, turn and hold in one continuous physics rollout and fail at the first phase the object is nudged, dropped, slips or drifts.

tools.name: latch_snap_test
tools.title: Latch snap test
tools.summary: Pinches a latch box's straps shut, lifts the box by its lid, shakes it and prises the latches open; passes only if the nubs sit in the windows throughout.
tools.description: Loads a box built by construct_latch_box in its 'seated' layout with the lid 12 mm above the rim, lets it drop, then runs the five measured phases of the asset's own proof without rendering: seat (n_latched must read 0, nothing holds the lid), close (a `close_force_N` pinch at each strap tip along the strap's rotating normal, with the equal and opposite force on the body; the strap must bow out over the nub and spring back), lift by the lid (capped PD force; the body must rise more than 40 mm with at least n-1 latches still engaged), shake (+-0.45 g sideways while hanging), and open (the reversed pinch; every latch must release). tools.name: model_finite_check

This verifier tests hypotheses instead: for each candidate joint it sets the joint to its open limit, renders the scene from the camera registered to the video, and correlates the edge map of that render with the edge map of a real frame taken while the part was moving, inside the image footprint the candidates occupy. tools.name: pad_press_slide_test
tools.title: Pad press-and-slide test
tools.summary: Lays a compliant pad (sponge, scrubber, eraser) on a floor, presses its top with a palm-like force, then drags it sideways below and above the friction limit: it must squash at its built stiffness, hold under the light drag, slide flat and in contact under the strong drag, and spring back on release.
tools.description: Loads the asset (built dict with `xml`, or an MJCF path), adds a floor plane with friction `floor_friction` and finds the free root body and the compliant slide joints in its subtree (the foam cells). inputs.name: min_slide_m

inputs.name: max_tilt_deg

inputs.name: min_contact_frac

tools.name: penetration_check
tools.title: Penetration check
tools.summary: Deepest interpenetration of every geom pair over a state or trajectory, on all visible geometry, optionally relative to a reference trajectory.
tools.description: Loads an MJCF scene and recompiles it with every visible geom collidable, so that parts a scene normally draws but does not collide, such as arm links, are checked as well. A pair fails when its depth exceeds the tolerance; with a reference trajectory it fails only when it exceeds the depth the same pair reaches in the reference plus the tolerance, so contacts the verified episode already had (a grasp, a seated object) are not counted as new collisions. inputs.name: qpos

inputs.name: baseline_qpos
inputs.description: Reference trajectory. Each pair may penetrate as deep as it does here, plus the tolerance.

inputs.name: tolerance
inputs.description: Penetration allowed beyond the reference, or in absolute terms without one. Default 0.003.

inputs.name: limbs
inputs.description: Groups of body names whose members are not checked against each other, for example one arm with its hand. Child bodies are included.

inputs.name: ignore
inputs.description: Regular expressions; a geom pair is skipped when either geom's 'body/geom' name matches one of them.

inputs.name: visual_groups
inputs.description: MuJoCo geom groups that count as visible. Default [0, 1, 2].

inputs.name: stride
inputs.description: Check every n-th frame. Default 1.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok (bool); violations: the failing pairs, worst first, each with the two 'body/geom' names, depth, excess over the reference and the frame; worst: the single worst pair; n_pairs_touching; n_frames; n_geoms_made_collidable; tolerance.

tools.name: plug_port_retention_test
tools.title: Plug-port insertion and retention test
tools.summary: Pushes a standard plug into a built receptacle with a capped force, then loads it outward, ramps a pull-out force and tries a misaligned push: the plug must seat, stay seated by friction, come out under a hand-sized pull and be blocked when off the slot.
tools.description: Loads the asset XML of a device with a declared port (a build dict with xml, body and port: {width, height, depth, mouth_local, axis_local}), holds the device kinematically at the origin (as a hand would) and adds a free plug: a box tip sized to the port minus a clearance on a larger housing that stops at the edge face. Four force-only trials with gravity on: (1) insert: an axial push of insert_force_N for insert_s from 3 mm outside the mouth must reach seat_frac of the cavity depth; (2) hold: with the push removed and an outward load of hold_load_N plus gravity along the pull direction (port facing down, the worst case), the tip must still be min_held_depth_m deep after hold_s (creep beyond max_slip_m is reported as a warning); (3) extract: an outward force ramped to max_extract_N must pull the plug out (a friction fit, not a weld) at no less than min_extract_N (the friction hold); (4) blocked: a plug offset sideways by one port width must not enter deeper than 0.5 mm. Assumes the device is a rigid body with the port as a cavity in its collision geometry.

inputs.name: tip_clearance_m

inputs.name: housing_scale

inputs.name: housing_len

inputs.name: plug_mass

inputs.name: seat_frac

inputs.name: min_held_depth_m
inputs.description: After the hold the tip must still be at least this deep in the cavity. Default 0.001

inputs.name: hold_load_N
inputs.description: Outward load during the hold (cord weight). Default 0.3

inputs.name: hold_s

inputs.name: max_slip_m

inputs.name: max_extract_N

tools.name: pump_stroke_test

tools.summary: Pushes a sprung slide joint (a spray pump head, a push button, a plunger) along its axis with a capped force: it must rest on its stop, resist a sub-preload push, follow its spring rate, bottom out under a finger force and spring back, for several cycles.

The moving body's weight is included in the applied force. Reports every displacement and the verdict; never raises on a bad mechanism.

tools.name: scissors_cut_test
tools.title: Scissors cut test
tools.summary: Pushes the rings of a built pair of scissors with a capped force and checks that the blades open, shut, and really sever a cord laid in the wedge.
tools.description: Builds a trial scene from the scissors asset: the pair on the floor with its blades set open, and (with cord=True) a cuttable rope laid across the wedge perpendicular to its bisector at `cut_frac` of the blade length, the rope's cut join at the crossing. The scissors driver then holds the tool in place with a gentle in-plane grip and squeezes the upper ring with up to 0.7 N; nothing writes the hinge. Every step try_sever measures the join against the blades and deactivates the join's equality only when the join is in the blades' span, in the wedge, in their plane, within cut_catch_m of the blade line, the hinge is closing, and both blades bite at least cut_pinch_mm with the edges closed to within the cord's diameter. Reports the opening reached, the smallest edge gap at the cord, and the cut record (blade gap and distance from the pivot at the moment it parted). With cord=False the pair starts shut, is opened by the ring force and must reach 60% of its range.

inputs.name: cord

outputs.description: The assembled trial scene, for inspection.

tools.name: settle_stability_check
tools.title: Settle stability check
tools.summary: Simulates the scene for a few seconds from its initial state; no free body may drift, fall or tip over.
tools.description: An object reconstructed at rest must stay at rest. The scene is stepped from its initial state for `seconds` (2 s by default) and every body with a free joint is measured against where it started: translation and rotation. A body that moves more than `drift_fail` (5 cm) or turns more than `rot_fail_deg` (30 degrees) fails; a body that moves more than `drift_warn` (1.5 cm) is reported as a warning. A translation with little rotation points at a placement error (the object hovers or sinks); a rotation beyond 90 degrees points at a wrong fitted orientation (it tips over). A diverging simulation is a failure of its own. The settled state is also returned so other checks can read it.

inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.description: Settle time. Default 2.0.

inputs.name: bodies
inputs.description: Free bodies to judge; all of them when omitted.

inputs.name: drift_fail
inputs.description: Translation that fails. Default 0.05.

inputs.name: rot_fail_deg
inputs.description: Rotation that fails. Default 30.

inputs.name: drift_warn
inputs.description: Translation that is reported as a warning. Default 0.015.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; drift: {body: {pos_m, rot_deg, verdict}}; failures and warnings as lists of body names; diverged (bool); settled_qpos: the state after settling.

tools.name: silhouette_iou_check
tools.title: Silhouette IoU check
tools.summary: Renders each object's silhouette from the video camera and compares it with the object's video mask; low IoU on one object means a wrong pose, on every object a wrong camera.
tools.description: The image-space proof that a reconstruction is registered to its footage. The scene is rendered with MuJoCo's segmentation renderer from the named camera at the resolution of the masks, each object's body (or the union of the bodies that make up a constructed object: the named body with its whole subtree, or every body matched by name prefix) becomes a silhouette, and its intersection over union with the given video mask is computed. An object below `min_iou` (0.25) fails; below `warn_iou` (0.45) is reported. When two or more objects are checked and all of them fail at once, the verifier reports `camera_suspect`: the camera they are all seen through is wrong, and re-fitting poses cannot help. The render and the masks must be the same aspect ratio, so the render is sized to the mask.

inputs.description: MJCF file, XML string, or compiled model.

inputs.name: masks
inputs.description: Object name -> binary mask (bool/uint8 array or PNG path), all the same size.

inputs.name: camera
inputs.description: Named camera in the scene, or a free camera {lookat, distance, azimuth, elevation}.

inputs.name: qpos
inputs.description: State to render; the initial state when omitted.

inputs.name: min_iou

inputs.name: warn_iou
inputs.description: Warning threshold. Default 0.45.

inputs.name: out_dir
inputs.description: If given, writes render.png and one overlay per object there.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; iou: {object: value}; failures; warnings; camera_suspect; bodies_used: which bodies formed each silhouette; render_size.

tools.name: soft_squeeze_test
tools.title: Soft squeeze test
tools.summary: Presses a soft free body onto a floor with a ramp of forces and checks that it compresses by a grasp-sized amount at a reference force, monotonically, and springs back when released.
tools.description: Loads the asset MJCF, adds a floor plane (with the given floor solref, default MuJoCo's 0.02 1) when none is present, settles the object for settle_s, records its rest height, then applies each downward force of `forces_N` to the body's centre of mass for hold_s and records the sink (rest z minus loaded z of the body origin, in mm). Passes when the state stays finite, the sink grows with force (within 0.3 mm), the sink at ref_force_N is within [min_mm, max_mm], the object does not tunnel below the floor by more than max_mm at the largest force, and after release it returns to within recover_mm of the rest height. The measurement is the compliance a pinch would feel, combined with the floor's own contact parameters (MuJoCo mixes the two geoms' solref). It does not simulate fabric deformation; it judges contact compliance.

inputs.name: min_mm
inputs.description: Least sink at the reference force. Default 2.

inputs.name: max_mm
inputs.description: Largest acceptable sink at any force. Default 25.

inputs.name: recover_mm
inputs.description: Allowed residual sink after release. Default 1.

inputs.name: settle_s
inputs.description: Settling time. Default 1.0.

inputs.name: hold_s
inputs.description: Time at each force. Default 0.6.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Optional report path.

outputs.description: All checks passed.

outputs.name: issues
outputs.description: What failed and which parameter to change.

outputs.name: compression_mm
outputs.description: Sink in mm per force.

outputs.name: rest_z_m
outputs.description: Settled body origin height.

outputs.name: recovered_mm
outputs.description: Residual sink after release.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: One sentence.

tools.name: spring_stiffness_test
tools.title: Spring stiffness test
tools.summary: Quasi-static force ramp on a built spring: measured N/m against the requested stiffness, plus a 10x overload check of the solid stop.
tools.description: Loads a spring built by construct_spring, presses its tip plate with each force in `forces` for 6 s of sim time, reads the compression, fits a line through the points still on the spring (under 85% of the travel) and reports the slope as the measured stiffness with its error against the requested value. It then presses with ten times the largest force and requires the compression to stay within 0.3 mm of the design travel, which is what a coil-bound stop does and a soft joint limit does not. Passes when the stiffness error is within `tolerance_pct` and the stop holds.

inputs.description: Allowed |measured - requested| / requested in percent. Default 15.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.description: Stiffness within tolerance and the solid stop holds.

outputs.name: verdict

tools.name: support_check
tools.title: Support check
tools.summary: After settling, every free body touches something, and every fixed object stands on a surface rather than hanging in mid-air or over an edge.
tools.description: Two ways an object can float. A free body that has no contact at all after the scene settles has fallen out of the world or hovers where no support was built. A fixed body, which the settle test cannot expose because it never falls, is probed with downward rays across its footprint: most of the footprint must have a surface directly below (`min_supported_frac`, 60 percent), and that surface must be close (`max_gap`, 15 mm). Static bodies whose name matches `support_names` (the table, the floor) are the supports themselves and are skipped. The report gives, per object, the supported fraction, the gap and the footprint, which is enough to decide whether to move the object or extend the surface.

tools.name: table_clearance_check
tools.title: Table clearance check
tools.summary: Lowest point of a carried body stays above the table top and above other bodies it passes over during the carry.

With obstacles (body names, or every non-robot body by default) it also requires that whenever the carried body's footprint overlaps an obstacle's footprint in XY, its lowest point is above that obstacle's top. tools.name: thread_self_locking_test
tools.title: Thread self-locking test
tools.summary: Force-only trial of a screw cap: straight push/pull must not move it, a twist must unscrew it along the full thread, then it must come free.
tools.description: Loads a bottle built by construct_bottle, seats the cap at the top of the thread (or leaves it as compiled with start='seated'), and runs the bottle driver: settle, push 20 N straight down, twist 0.1 N*m closed, pull 20 N straight up, twist open until the thread runs out, lift the free cap away, drop it. Only xfrc_applied is written. It measures the cap travel without turning, the pitch coupling error between lift and yaw, the turns applied, and how far the twist actually got before the thread released. TWIST STALLED means the cap jammed (contact interference or friction); NOT A THREAD means straight force alone moved the cap. The same trial runs on any asset that exposes the bottle contract: bodies cap/bottle/carrier, joints yaw/lift, equalities thread/engaged and total_lift_m.

tools.name: urdf_articulation_check
tools.title: URDF articulation check
tools.summary: A URDF describes a real mechanism: valid joint types with limits, links with geometry, and mesh-based visuals rather than a few primitive boxes typed by hand.
tools.description: When a construction tool keeps rejecting its inputs, the easy escape is to type a URDF by hand: three boxes and an invalid joint type that count as 'articulated' while looking nothing like the object. This verifier parses the URDF and decides from its structure: every joint type must be one URDF defines; at least `min_moving_joints` joints must be prismatic, revolute or continuous, with finite limits where the type needs them; every link must have geometry; and, unless `allow_primitives` is set, the visual geometry must include meshes, because a measured reconstruction is never only primitives. Mesh files referenced by the URDF must exist next to it. The report lists joints with their types and limits and the reasons for any failure.

inputs.name: urdf_path
inputs.description: The URDF file.

inputs.name: min_moving_joints
inputs.description: Prismatic/revolute/continuous joints required. Default 1.

inputs.name: allow_primitives
inputs.description: Accept a URDF whose visuals are only boxes, cylinders and spheres. Default False.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; joints: [{name, type, parent, child, limits}]; links: count; mesh_files: found and missing; reasons: why it failed.

tools.name: vessel_containment_test
tools.title: Vessel containment test
tools.summary: Drops the vessel (lands upright), drops a ball into it (stays inside, below the rim) and optionally a second vessel (nests inside); gravity only.
tools.description: Loads the vessel asset and attaches a ball (radius 0.4 x the inner rim radius by default, capped at 2 cm) and, with inner_built, the second vessel's XML under a prefix. Trial 1 lifts the vessel 2 cm and lets it fall for 1.5 s: its z axis must stay within 15 degrees of vertical and its base within 5 mm of the floor. Trial 2 releases the ball 3 cm above the rim centre and after 2 s requires it inside: horizontal distance from the vessel axis under the inner rim radius minus the ball radius, centre below the rim and above the inner floor. Trial 3 releases the inner vessel's base 1 cm above the rim and requires its base site to end below the outer rim and its axis upright. Reports every number; passes when all requested trials pass.

inputs.name: built
inputs.description: The dict construct_cup/construct_bowl returned, or the path of its <name>_params.json.

inputs.name: inner_built
inputs.description: A second vessel to nest inside (its rim must fit through this one's mouth).

inputs.name: ball_radius
inputs.description: Test ball radius; default 0.4 x inner rim radius, max 2 cm.

inputs.name: out_json
inputs.description: Write the report here.

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: All trials passed.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: One sentence with the measured numbers.

outputs.name: measured
outputs.description: drop {tilt_deg, base_height_mm, ok}, fill {ball_off_axis_mm, ball_z_mm, below_rim, above_floor, ok}, nest {inner_base_below_rim_mm, tilt_deg, ok} when requested.

tools.name: weld_gap_check
tools.title: Weld gap check
tools.summary: Position and angle residual of every active weld or connect constraint on every frame.
tools.description: For each active weld (or connect) equality constraint in the scene, replays the trajectory kinematically and measures how far the two anchor points are apart and, for a weld with a rotational part, the angle between the two frames. Fails when the gap exceeds 5 mm or the angle 3 degrees anywhere, the tolerance below which a physics replay starts without a visible snap. Constraints can be selected by body name pattern; by default all are checked. Works on any scene that uses equality constraints to assemble a robot or an object.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz or qpos array.

inputs.name: gap_tol_m
inputs.description: Largest allowed anchor separation. Default 0.005.

inputs.name: angle_tol_deg
inputs.description: Largest allowed frame misalignment for torque-carrying welds. Default 3.

inputs.name: only
inputs.description: fnmatch patterns on either body name; others are skipped.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; per constraint: bodies, max gap (mm), max angle (deg), worst frame and label, position-only flag.

tools.name: wrist_servo_offset_check
tools.title: Wrist servo offset check
tools.summary: Measure the steady-state error of the hand's wrist position servos at a pose with the fingers closed, and return the command offset that cancels it.
tools.description: The wrist actuators are position servos with steady-state error under load: a solved grasp pose can sit 7 mm low once the hand hangs on it dynamically, which lifts the pads clear of a cord while every static measurement still says the pose is seated. The hand is driven to the pose for `steps` steps, the error between commanded and reached wrist position is read, the command is corrected by it, and this repeats for a few rounds. The offset is kept only while it helps: if the error does not shrink (the hand is blocked by the table, not lagging) the search stops and the best offset so far is returned. Passes when the residual error is below tol_mm. Measure it with the hand CLOSED: the same grasp reads -1.7 mm open and +7.3 mm closed.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: {hand_xml, side, objects, floor}

inputs.name: pose
inputs.description: {pos, euler, finger_targets}

inputs.name: tol_mm
inputs.description: acceptable residual (default 1.5)

inputs.name: steps / rounds
inputs.description: settle steps per round (250) and rounds (3)

inputs.name: give_up_mm
inputs.description: offset beyond which the hand is considered blocked (default 15)

outputs.name: ok
outputs.description: residual error below tol_mm

outputs.name: offset_m
outputs.description: subtract from the commanded wrist position

outputs.name: residual_mm
outputs.description: error after correction

outputs.name: raw_error_mm
outputs.description: error with no correction

tools.name: wrist_spin_check
tools.title: Wrist spin check
tools.summary: Largest monotone turn of each wrist joint stays under 180 degrees and the joint does not wander back and forth.
tools.description: Splits each named hinge trajectory into monotone runs (ignoring reversals smaller than the noise floor) and reports the largest run in degrees, failing when it reaches the spin limit (180 degrees by default). It also counts reversals larger than redundant_deg (15 degrees by default) that happen inside one phase label; a wrist that turns 30 degrees one way and back within the same phase did not need to turn. Joints default to every hinge whose name contains 'roll' or ends in the last arm joint index; pass them explicitly for other robots.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz or qpos array; phase labels enable the redundancy rule.

inputs.name: joints
inputs.description: Hinge joints to check. Default: hinges with 'roll', 'j6' or 'wrist' in their name.

inputs.name: spin_limit_deg
inputs.description: Largest monotone turn allowed. Default 180.

inputs.name: redundant_deg
inputs.description: A reversal this large inside one phase counts as redundant turning. Default 15.

inputs.name: noise_deg
inputs.description: Reversals below this are jitter. Default 1.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; per joint: largest turn, its frames and labels, net turn, redundant reversals (frame, size, label).

tools.name: wrist_stop_check
tools.title: Wrist stop check
tools.summary: Named joints stay inside the real hardware's ranges, with a margin, on every frame.
tools.description: Compares each named joint's trajectory against the range the real hardware can reach (degrees for hinges, metres for slides), minus a safety margin, and fails on any frame outside it. By default it finds the wrist hinges by name (roll, wrist, j6) and uses the scene's own joint limits; pass joints={name: (lo, hi)} with the real stops, or real_stops={side: (lo, hi)} to apply one range per side by name. The report gives each joint's minimum and maximum, the remaining margin to each stop and the frame and phase label of the closest approach. The module carries the real wrist-roll stops the paper's arms were deployed with, right (-20, 180) and left (-180, 20) degrees, as REAL_WRIST_STOPS_DEG.

inputs.name: scene
inputs.description: MJCF scene.

inputs.name: trajectory
inputs.description: trajectory.npz or qpos array.

inputs.name: joints
inputs.type: dict joint name -> (lo, hi) | list[str] | None
inputs.description: Joints to check with their real ranges (degrees for hinges). A list uses the model's limits; None finds wrist hinges by name.

inputs.name: real_stops
inputs.description: Real range applied to each default joint whose name contains the side.

inputs.name: margin_deg
inputs.description: Reserve kept from each explicit real range. Default 2; the model's own limits get 0.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: ok; per joint: min, max, range, margin to each stop, worst frame and label.
